intake.q: Who was the person to you?
Which state did the death happen in?
Has the death been registered yet?
Were they working, retired, or neither?
Was a vehicle registered in their name?
Did they have a life insurance policy?

nodes.title: Register the death
nodes.summary: 21 days. After that there are late fees and extra paperwork.
nodes.body: Death registration is governed by the Registration of Births and Deaths Act. Registration within 21 days is the normal route; later registration attracts fees and additional process. Which portal serves you depends on your state — the central CRS portal covers a named list of states and Karnataka is not on it.
documents: Medical certificate of cause of death

warnings.text: The national CRS portal does not cover every state. Check yours before creating an account.

nodes.sourceLabel: Registration of Births and Deaths Act

nodes.title: Order several certified copies at once
nodes.summary: Most offices keep a copy. Ordering once saves repeat trips.
nodes.body: Each institution you approach will retain a certified copy. Requesting several in one application avoids returning to the registrar repeatedly.

nodes.title: Claim the bank balance
nodes.summary: With a nominee registered, the bank cannot ask for a court order.
nodes.body: Where a nominee is registered, the bank must release the balance on a claim form, the death certificate and ID. It cannot insist on a succession certificate, probate or an indemnity bond, whatever the amount. Important: the nominee receives the money as a trustee, not as owner. The funds still belong to the legal heirs under the applicable succession law.

warnings.text: Being the nominee does not make you the owner. You hold it for the legal heirs.

nodes.title: Claim the bank balance without a nominee
nodes.summary: Your bank sets its own limit. Ask before assuming you need a court.
nodes.body: Below the bank's own threshold: a claim form signed by all claimants, the death certificate, ID, a bond of indemnity, and a letter of disclaimer or no-objection from any heir not claiming. Above it: a succession certificate, letter of administration or probate. RBI requires each bank to fix its own threshold and they vary enormously — one major bank sets it at ₹40 lakh, another at ₹15 lakh. Ask yours first.
nodes.typicalDays: weeks, or months if a court is involved
documents: Claim form signed by all claimants
Letter of disclaimer from heirs not claiming

warnings.text: If the heirs disagree, the bank will require a court order even below its threshold.

nodes.title: Get a legal heir or succession certificate
nodes.summary: Two different documents. The faster one isn't accepted everywhere.
nodes.body: A Legal Heir Certificate comes from the Tahsildar and is faster, roughly one to three months, but not every bank accepts it. A Succession Certificate comes from the District Civil Court under the Indian Succession Act 1925 — petition, public notice in a local newspaper, affidavits, court fee — and takes several months.
nodes.typicalDays: one to three months, or several for the court route

warnings.text: Ask the bank which of the two it accepts before you start. They are not interchangeable.

nodes.title: Claim the provident fund
nodes.summary: Form 20. Death claims are processed offline, not online.
nodes.body: Form 20 claims the PF balance. Submit it with the original death certificate, a cancelled cheque or passbook of the claimant, the claimant's Aadhaar, and a guardianship certificate where a non-parent claims for a minor. If no e-nomination was filed, the amount is distributed among surviving family members as defined under the EPF Scheme; where no family exists, a succession certificate is required.
documents: Guardianship certificate if claiming for a minor

warnings.text: Death claims cannot be filed on the online portal. This one is offline.

nodes.title: Claim the family pension
nodes.summary: Form 10D. A monthly pension for life if they had ten years of service.
nodes.body: Ten years of service is the minimum for a monthly pension. Widow pension is calculated as pensionable salary multiplied by pensionable service, divided by 70, with a statutory floor of ₹1,000 a month under the 2014 amendment. Children's pension is 25% of the widow pension per child, for a maximum of two children at a time, until age 25 — for life where the child has 40% or more disability. Entitlement goes to spouse and children first; parents can claim only where there is no surviving spouse and no children. Under ten years of service there is no monthly pension, but a withdrawal benefit from EPS applies, plus the full PF accumulation and EDLI.

nodes.title: Claim the EDLI insurance — most families never do
nodes.summary: Between ₹2.5 lakh and ₹7 lakh. The employee never paid a rupee for it.
nodes.body: Every EPF member is automatically insured under EDLI. It is funded entirely by an employer contribution of 0.5% of wages — nothing is deducted from the employee, which is why almost nobody knows it exists. The payout ranges from a minimum of ₹2.5 lakh to a maximum of ₹7 lakh since the 2021 enhancement, and it is exempt from tax under section 10(10D). Claim it with Form 5IF alongside Forms 20 and 10D.

nodes.title: If the employer won't sign the forms
nodes.summary: You can file directly. These are statutory rights, not favours.
nodes.body: Employers sometimes refuse to attest death claim forms, often because of an unrelated full-and-final settlement dispute. Forms 20, 10D and 5IF can be submitted directly to the Regional Provident Fund Commissioner with a covering letter explaining the employer's non-cooperation. PF, EPS and EDLI are statutory entitlements and an employer cannot withhold them.

nodes.title: Transfer the vehicle
nodes.summary: Tell the RTO within 30 days. Apply within 3 months.
nodes.body: Under Rule 56(3) of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules 1989, the person succeeding to possession of the vehicle may use it for three months as if it had been transferred to them, provided they inform the registering authority within thirty days of the death and of their intention to use it. The transfer application itself is Form 31, filed within those three months. Form 31 is for a death — Forms 29 and 30 are for a sale, and the two get confused constantly.

warnings.text: The 30-day intimation is separate from the 3-month application. Missing the first one costs you the right to use the vehicle in the meantime.

statutoryClock.label: Inform the RTO
statutoryClock.consequence: loss of the interim right to use the vehicle

nodes.title: Deactivate their Aadhaar
nodes.summary: An active Aadhaar after death is a fraud surface.
nodes.body: UIDAI runs a Reporting of Death of a Family Member service on the myAadhaar portal, live since June 2025 and currently covering 25 states and union territories with the rest being integrated. A family member self-authenticates and supplies the deceased's Aadhaar number and the death registration number from the certificate.

nodes.title: File the life insurance claim
nodes.summary: There is a statutory deadline once you've given them everything.
nodes.body: Insurers work to a regulatory deadline once they have received all documents and clarifications. That deadline was tightened recently and sources disagree on the current figure, so ask your insurer for their stated timeline in writing at the point of intimation and hold them to it. Intimate the claim first — it registers the claim and starts the clock, and it does not require documents.

warnings.text: Intimate first, gather documents second. Intimation starts the clock and needs nothing.
